subject: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit.patel@fintechx.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria

Hi Amit / Priya,

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the walkthrough of FintechX's inference workload and the goals you outlined. Per our call, I’m sending a concise POC observability plan and proposed success criteria so we can align on the evaluation path and owners.

High-level recap (from call):
- POC scope: 2 production-like routes (auth + transaction-enrichment) running ~150 TPS peaks, mixed short/long prompts.
- Goals: confirm latency SLOs, verify cost-per-op improvements with batching/caching, and validate end-to-end reliability under simulated production traffic.

Proposed success criteria (we'll attach a spreadsheet with details):
- Latency: p95 latency <= 250ms for auth route and <= 500ms for enrichment under target load.
- Error budget: <1% 5xx rate; graceful degradation with fallback to smaller model when resource constrained.
- Cost: >=20% reduction in per-token inference cost vs current baseline with configured batching/quantization.
- Quality: no more than 3% regression in NIST-style scoring on the provided eval set.

Observability plan (what we'll instrument and review):
- Dashboards: per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), request rate, concurrency, token count distribution.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces from FintechX frontend through Redwood routing to model execution to measure queue + exec latency.
- Logs & exports: structured request/response logs (sampled), error logs with stack/context, and KV cache hit/miss metrics.
- Metrics to monitor: model exec time, queue time, batch size, GPU utilization, memory pressure, inference error rates, model-variant fallback counts.

Evaluation plan & timelines:
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and share access for log/metrics export.
2) Week 1: provisioning + instrumentation (we provide dashboards and tracing hooks).
3) Week 2: ramp test traffic; first validation of latency and cost metrics.
4) Week 3: tuning (batching/quantization) and final readout.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (POC owner) & Jordan (SRE/observability).
- FintechX: Amit (POC sponsor) & Priya (tech lead).

Attachments: poc-success-criteria.xlsx (detailed metrics and thresholds), observability-dashboard-mock.png (dashboard mockups).

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm the success criteria above or suggest edits by EOD Friday.
- Provide a sample of production request traces or a small sample log export (redacted) so we can validate field mappings.
- Confirm a 60–90 minute kickoff Tues/Wed next week for provisioning and walkthrough.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites once we have dates.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Quick clarifications from our side:
1) For latency we care most about p95 under sustained load (not just bursts) — can you confirm the p95 target is measured over a 5 minute sliding window?
2) Quality: when you say NIST-style scoring, can you include an example evaluation script or the metric you’ll use so Priya's team can reproduce?
3) Log export: we can provide a 48-hour redacted log dump (JSON lines) by tomorrow afternoon. Is that sufficient?

Agree with the proposed timeline. One additional ask: we track retention and data residency for logs (30-day retention, US only). Please note for the POC — we'll need to ensure exported logs are stored in our GCP bucket in us-central1.

Proposed kickoff: Tue Nov 17 10:00 AM ET — does that work for Redwood?

Amit
Director of Engineering, FintechX
amit.patel@fintechx.com
